# AOS Migration Plan

**Target repo**: `/Users/oscarrieken/Projects/Rieken/ai-assistant-dot-files`
**Source of truth**: `docs/aos/AOS_Governance_Design_Pack/`
**Migration principle**: Expand/Contract (per `shared/rules/architecture-guardrails.md` #2) — add AOS layers alongside current framework; never remove or rename anything current teams depend on until adoption is real.
**Backward-compatibility guarantee**: a team on any prior version that upgrades to any AOS milestone without adopting any AOS-specific feature MUST see zero behavior change in what they use today.
**Generated by**: architectural planning session — 2026-07-22

---

## Current State vs AOS Vision

The AOS design pack names **six principles** (Capability, Governance, Learning, Memory Engineering, Context Engineering, Continuous Improvement). Scoring the current framework against them:

| Principle | Current coverage | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Capability | ✓ Strong — 28+ skills, 20+ agents, blueprints, rules | None material |
| Context Engineering | ✓ Moderate — `context-engineer` skill + agent, `search-ki`, `query-memory` | Context Auditor role missing; lexical retrieval only |
| Memory Engineering | ✓ Partial — KIs, ADRs, `shared/memory-registry.json`, `promote-memory`, `extract-lessons` | No forgetting engine; no expansion/compression pair; lexical retrieval only |
| Governance | ⚠ Weak — approval gates in prose rules (`approval-gates.md`); no runtime enforcement | 15 producer/counter role pairs missing; no policy layer |
| Learning | ⚠ Weak — retrospective + promote-memory (manual triggers) | No continuous learning engine; no automated curation loop |
| Continuous Improvement | ⚠ Weak — `agent-scorecard`, `pipeline-retrospective`, `context-audit` (all ad-hoc skills) | No first-class evaluation runtime; telemetry limited to `pipeline-trace.json` |

The design pack's **suggested `.project-ai/` directory** adds layers the current framework doesn't have as first-class:
- `hooks/`, `orchestration/`, `evaluation/`, `telemetry/`, `rag/`, `schemas/`

The design pack's **15 governance pairs** (from `01-Governance-Checks-and-Balances.md`):

| # | Producer | Counter | Producer exists today? | Counter exists today? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Context Engineer | Context Auditor | ✓ agent+skill | ✗ |
| 2 | Memory Engineer | Memory Auditor | ✓ agent | ✗ |
| 3 | Knowledge Curator | Knowledge Auditor | ✗ (closest: `create-ki` skill) | ✗ |
| 4 | Prompt Architect | Prompt Evaluator | ✗ (implicit — humans) | ✗ |
| 5 | Agent Designer | Agent Evaluator | ✗ (implicit — humans) | partial (`agent-eval` skill) |
| 6 | Rule Author | Rule Auditor | ✗ (implicit — humans) | ✗ |
| 7 | Pattern Author | Pattern Reviewer | ✗ (implicit — humans) | ✗ |
| 8 | Tool Builder | Tool Validator | ✗ (implicit — humans) | ✗ |
| 9 | Documentation Writer | Documentation Auditor | ✓ `tech-writer` agent | ✗ |
| 10 | Retrieval Engine | Retrieval Evaluator | partial (`search-ki` skill) | ✗ |
| 11 | Memory Expansion | Memory Compression | ✗ | ✗ |
| 12 | Learning Engine | Forgetting Engine | ✗ | ✗ |
| 13 | Cost Optimizer | Quality Optimizer | ✗ | ✗ |
| 14 | Security Reviewer | Privacy Auditor | ✓ `security-reviewer` agent | ✗ |
| 15 | Orchestrator | Scheduler | partial (`deliver-feature` skill) | ✗ |

11 pairs are **audit relationships** (producer + auditor). 4 pairs are **opposing forces** (Memory Expansion ↔ Compression, Learning ↔ Forgetting, Cost ↔ Quality, Orchestrator ↔ Scheduler). Migration handles them differently.

---

## Migration Principles

1. **Every AOS addition is opt-in.** If a team doesn't invoke a new skill/agent, nothing behaves differently.
2. **Directory namespaces coexist.** Keep `.claude/` unchanged; if AOS wants a new namespace, add it as an alias or optional subdirectory — never rename.
3. **Version bumps signal scope.** Minor bumps for additions; major bump only when the base framework's default behavior changes (not planned in this migration).
4. **Install script gains modes.** `--base` (current framework only, existing behavior) and `--full` (AOS layers included). Default stays `--base` initially; flip to `--full` in a future v4.
5. **Telemetry is fire-and-forget-optional.** Never required for pipeline correctness.
6. **Counter agents run only when invoked.** They may be invoked automatically by `validate-artifact` when configured, but the default remains "structural check only."
7. **Documentation ordering is enforced.** README says "the base framework is X; AOS layers are optional and documented in `docs/aos/`."

## Phase 1 — Foundations (v3.0, purely additive, zero risk)

**Goal**: land the telemetry + evaluation infrastructure and ONE counter agent as the pattern exemplar. Everything invocable but skippable.

- [ ] **Op 1.1**: Create `shared/telemetry/` with:
  - [ ] `README.md` — what telemetry captures, opt-in nature, retention policy
  - [ ] `event-schema.md` — JSON schema for pipeline events (agent invoked, artifact written, validation passed/failed, etc.)
  - [ ] `event-recorder.md` skill — minimal recorder writing events to `.claude/telemetry/events.jsonl`
- [ ] **Op 1.2**: Create `shared/evaluation/` with:
  - [ ] `README.md` — evaluation model: continuous vs on-demand
  - [ ] Move `pipeline-retrospective` skill's spec into an evaluation config; keep the skill working exactly as today
- [ ] **Op 1.3**: Create first counter agent as pattern exemplar:
  - [ ] `shared/agents/memory-auditor.md` — audits changes to `shared/knowledge/` and `.claude/knowledge/` for KI schema compliance, duplicate detection, stale-tag flags
  - [ ] Version starts at `1.0.0`; agent frontmatter follows existing conventions
- [ ] **Op 1.4**: Update `shared/skills/health-check/SKILL.md` to detect + report AOS layers if present (opt-in section in report)
- [ ] **Op 1.5**: Update `shared/agents/CHANGELOG.md` with v3.0 entry listing additions
- [ ] **Op 1.6**: Add `docs/aos/migration-guide.md` — the "how to opt in" doc; empty in v3.0 since nothing forces adoption yet
- [ ] **Op 1.7**: Verify: fresh install of v3.0 with zero AOS invocation produces identical pipeline output to v2.x on a known feature

**Exit criterion**: `git tag v3.0.0` is safe to publish; a team upgrading and doing nothing new sees zero change.

**Rollback plan**: `git revert` the phase's commits — all additions are in new files/directories, nothing modifies existing behavior paths.

- [ ] **Op 3.8**: Write `docs/aos/migration-guide.md` proper — how to opt in per layer

### Trinity-native workflow refactor (part of Phase 3)

These three ops apply the Tool/Persona/Workflow trinity (established in saturday-mcp) to the framework itself. Skills that currently orchestrate agents become thin callers of first-class Workflows; agents that hold multi-step loops internally get those loops extracted into Workflows.

- [ ] **Op 3.11**: Refactor `/deliver-feature` skill's orchestration logic into a `FeatureDeliveryWorkflow`. Skill becomes a thin caller; workflow owns the state machine (named internal roles for analyst/architect/developer/reviewer/qa/tech-writer/devops, resumable checkpoints backed by `.claude/feature-workspace/` state, explicit stage boundaries where policy evaluation can hook in later in Phase 4). External invocation contract stays identical — teams keep typing `/deliver-feature <spec>`.
- [ ] **Op 3.12**: Extract the Red-Green-Refactor loop from `test-driven-developer` agent into a `TDDWorkflow`. Internal roles: test-writer (played by `unit-tester`), implementer (played by `developer`), refactor-reviewer (played by `developer` + `code-reviewer` audit), coverage-auditor (played by `unit-tester` in audit mode). Agent becomes a thin caller; workflow owns the loop, retry policy, and coverage gates.
- [ ] **Op 3.13**: Establish "workflow-invokes-audit-after-producer" as the default composition pattern. Every workflow step that ends with a contract-bound artifact automatically invokes the corresponding counter agent from Phase 2 (e.g., `analyst` step → `context-auditor` audit → proceed or retry). Auditor-on-failure sends the artifact back to the producer with the specific violations. Config knob exists to disable per-project, but default is "audits run."

**Exit criterion**: the full AOS runtime exists and works; opt-in path documented; `/deliver-feature` and `/test-driven-developer` are now workflows (Tool/Persona/Workflow trinity applied to the framework itself).

**Rollback plan**: Learning/Forgetting are drafts-only by default (never auto-mutate memory). RAG runs alongside lexical, not instead of. Orchestration wraps, doesn't replace — the pre-workflow skill implementation stays available under a `--legacy` flag through v3.x so any team hitting a workflow-introduced regression can revert per-project without waiting for a framework patch.

## Phase 4 — Policy layer (v3.3)

**Goal**: telemetry + evaluation are now producing data; introduce optional policy files for auto-approval.

- [ ] **Op 4.1**: Design `shared/policies/` (or `shared/orchestration/policies/`):

  - [ ] Evaluates against telemetry events + agent outputs
  - [ ] Emits telemetry event for every policy decision (audit trail)
- [ ] **Op 4.3**: Add 3 sample policies covering common patterns:
  - [ ] `auto-approve-doc-changes.policy.yaml`
  - [ ] `auto-approve-test-additions.policy.yaml`
  - [ ] `require-human-review-security.policy.yaml`
- [ ] **Op 4.4**: Write `docs/aos/policy-authoring-guide.md`
- [ ] **Op 4.5**: Update `shared/rules/approval-gates.md` — add optional "policy-based" gate type alongside existing human-only gates
- [ ] **Op 4.6**: Update `health-check` to audit policy syntax + coverage
- [ ] **Op 4.7**: Update `CHANGELOG.md` with v3.3 entry

**Exit criterion**: policy layer works; every existing approval gate has a documented "here's the equivalent policy if you want it" recipe.

**Rollback plan**: policies are opt-in per-project. Default (no policies configured) is "all approvals require human confirmation" — identical to v2.x.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **[RISK-HIGH]** Adding 14 counter agents in Phase 2 doubles the `shared/agents/` directory size. Teams may feel the framework got heavier. Mitigate with strong README + `[AOS]` prefix in agent descriptions.
- **[RISK-MED]** RAG in Phase 3 requires a vector store choice (Qdrant vs pgvector vs LightRAG). Each has operational cost. Recommend LightRAG per the design pack; decision worth an ADR.
- **[RISK-MED]** The Learning engine could propose bad KIs at scale, causing memory bloat. Mitigate: drafts only, human approval required to persist.
- **[AMBIGUOUS]** The design pack names `Prompt Architect`, `Rule Author`, etc. as "producer" roles but they're implicit human roles today. Interpretation: their Auditor/Evaluator counters are automated agents that audit human-authored artifacts. Confirm this interpretation before Phase 2.
- **[ASSUMPTION]** `deliver-feature` skill remains the primary orchestration path for the base framework indefinitely. Orchestration runtime in Phase 3 wraps it; never replaces it.
- **[ASSUMPTION]** No breaking changes to existing agent/skill/rule locations. Any AOS addition that would require moving existing files gets deferred to a hypothetical v4.

---

## Downstream Agents

Each op above should be executed by:
1. **`developer`** — implements the new files (agents, skills, schemas)
2. **`code-reviewer`** — verifies pattern conformance (matches existing agent frontmatter, matches skill format, respects backward-compat)
3. **`tech-writer`** — updates README, CHANGELOG, migration-guide per phase

Per-phase specialists:
- Phase 1: `sre-engineer` reviews telemetry schema cardinality
- Phase 2: `security-reviewer` reviews privacy-auditor design
- Phase 3: `performance-engineer` reviews RAG retrieval latency budget
- Phase 4: `security-reviewer` reviews policy evaluator for privilege-escalation risks

Consider `/adr` for these decisions:
- Phase 1: telemetry event schema (append-only, JSONL vs structured)
- Phase 2: counter-agent invocation policy (auto vs opt-in)
- Phase 3: RAG backend (LightRAG vs pgvector vs Qdrant)
- Phase 4: policy schema language (YAML vs Rego vs OPA)

---

## Estimate

Rough scope: ~38 ops across 4 phases + ADRs + docs. If each op takes ~1-2 hours including tests + review, that's ~55-75 hours of focused work spread across 4 minor releases. Phase 3 grew from 10 to 13 ops with the trinity-native workflow refactor (3.11-3.13); Phase 3 is the heaviest phase.

Recommend one milestone per release cadence — e.g., 2-week releases means v3.0 ships in ~2 weeks after start, v3.1 two weeks later, etc. Total elapsed: ~2 months to reach v3.3.

**One milestone at a time. Never batch phases.** Each release must be independently useful and independently revertable.

---

## Success Criteria

The AOS migration is successful when:

1. **v3.3 is live** with all four phases landed.
2. **A team on v2.x can install v3.3 with `--base`** and see zero behavior change from what they use today.
3. **A team on v3.3 can opt in to `--full`** and use policy-based auto-approval to eliminate at least one class of "just-say-yes" human gate (e.g., doc-only changes).
4. **Telemetry-backed evaluations** replace ad-hoc `agent-scorecard` runs — improving/degrading agents are detected automatically.
5. **The Learning engine** proposes at least one KI candidate per month automatically from retrospectives, human-approved before persisting.
6. **The Forgetting engine** flags at least one stale KI per quarter for review.
7. **No skill, agent, or rule from v2.x is removed** — deprecated, maybe, but functional.

The migration deliberately does **NOT** aim for:
- Stage 4 (semi-autonomous delivery) — that would require removing human gates by default; AOS keeps them, just makes them policy-driven when opt-in.
- Replacing the base framework with the AOS runtime — the base stays as the "no AOS" path forever.
